description: Git : contrôle de version distribué — concepts fondamentaux, HEAD vs main, branches locales/distantes, git pull vs fetch (avec schémas).

questions.prompt: What is Git and what are its key features?
questions.answer_text:
Git is a distributed version control system (DVCS) that tracks changes to files and coordinates work between multiple people on a development project.

Key features:
- Version Control: tracks the complete history of changes, lets you revert to previous versions, and compare differences.
- Distributed System: each developer has a complete copy of the project, works offline, no single point of failure.
- Collaboration: multiple developers work simultaneously; Git merges compatible changes automatically and manages conflicts.

questions.prompt: What are the fundamental Git concepts (Repository, Commit, Branch, Merge, Clone)?
questions.answer_text:
- Repository: a folder containing your project and its Git history.
- Commit: a snapshot of your project at a given point in time.
- Branch: an independent line of development.
- Merge: merging two branches together.
- Clone: a local copy of a remote repository.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between HEAD and main (and attached vs detached HEAD)?
questions.answer_text:
HEAD is a pointer indicating where you currently are in your Git repository. There is only one HEAD per repository; it moves when you change branches or commits (it points to the commit you're working on).
main is the name of a branch — usually the main branch of the project.

- Attached HEAD (normal): HEAD → main → commit abc123 (HEAD points to a branch that points to a commit).
- Detached HEAD: HEAD → commit abc123 (HEAD points directly to a commit, not to a branch).

questions.prompt: What is the difference between main and origin/main?
questions.answer_text:
- main (local branch): your local branch that exists on your machine.
- origin/main (remote tracking branch): a local reference to the main branch of the remote repository (it reflects the last known state of the remote).

questions.prompt: What is the difference between git pull and git fetch?
questions.answer_text:
- git fetch: downloads the latest changes from the remote repository into your remote-tracking branches (e.g. origin/main), but does NOT modify your working branch. You can review before merging.
- git pull: does a git fetch AND then merges the changes into your current branch (git pull = git fetch + git merge). It updates your working branch immediately.
